experiments.title: How words and blame match lines from one version to the next
experiments.question: words took 79 s on Czechia sb/2007/378. 49 of 54 s were Python's difflib matching lines; it is quadratic in repeated lines, and half this statute's lines are blank. Six ways of matching lines were compared on 30 files: speed, and how many characters each credits to a different law than before.
experiments.result: git's histogram diff was the fastest and the closest to the old answers: 0.12% of characters credited differently, all in one file. Leaving blank lines out, patience anchoring and git's default (Myers) were 2 to 5% off. Adding move detection did not bring the answers closer.
experiments.decision: Kept: difflib as before for most files; git's histogram diff when both versions are long (over 1,000,000 line pairs); difflib if git cannot run. words on the 4 slow files: 76 s to 18 s; blame replay: 75 s to 10 s; 26 of 30 files give byte-identical answers. Open: text amended and moved in one version is credited to the amending law, by both methods.
